questions.q: Why did the consul think the robber might not come to the consulate at all?
choices: A robber does not like to leave traces of his flight behind
The consulate was too far away from the quay
The steamer would leave before the office opened
Robbers are always afraid of meeting the police
questions.evidence: A robber doesn't quite like to leave traces of his flight behind him

questions.q: What did Fix hope the consul would do with the stranger's passport?
choices: Keep it locked in the consulate safe
Refuse to visa it
Send it to Scotland Yard in London
Copy out every word of it for him
questions.evidence: I hope you will not visa the passport

questions.q: Why did the consul say he could not refuse to visa the passport?
choices: Fogg was a very rich and important gentleman
Fix had no proof that he was really a detective
If the passport was genuine, he had no right to refuse
The law said every passport must be signed at Suez
questions.evidence: If the passport is genuine I have no right to refuse.

questions.q: Why did Fogg want his passport visaed, even though no passport was required?
choices: To prove that he came by Suez
To be allowed to land later in Bombay
Because the steamer captain asked him to
To keep the police from following him
questions.evidence: I wish to prove, by your visa, that I came by Suez.

questions.q: What did the consul think of Fogg after meeting him?
choices: He seemed nervous and in a great hurry
He looked and acted like a perfectly honest man
He seemed rude and refused to answer any questions
He matched the robber in every single way
questions.evidence: he looks and acts like a perfectly honest man

questions.q: Why did Fix decide to go after Passepartout instead of Fogg?
choices: He thought the servant was the real robber
He thought the talkative servant would reveal more
He wanted to hire the clever servant to work for him
He needed the servant to carry a letter to London
questions.evidence: he's a Frenchman, and can't help talking

questions.q: What did Fogg's notebook show when he reached Suez?
choices: He was two days ahead of his time
He had lost half a day in Paris
He had neither gained nor lost any time
He was already one full day behind
questions.evidence: he had as yet neither gained nor lost

questions.q: What did Fogg do instead of looking around the town of Suez?
choices: He went to the bazaar to buy some new shirts
He sat down quietly to breakfast in his cabin
He wrote a long letter home to his friends
He walked up on deck to watch the boats come in
questions.evidence: He sat down quietly to breakfast in his cabin, never once thinking of inspecting the town
